name: Microsoft Busan Data Center 1 (Mieum/Miumsandan)
notes: First Microsoft datacenter in Busan, in the International Industrial Logistics City / Mieum (Miumsandan) foreign-investment zone, Gangseo-gu; announced 2014/2016 and launched April 2020, hosting Azure Korea South region cloud services. ~50 MW campus capacity reported by Korean trade blogs (unverified). Microsoft holds land rights for up to 6 data centers on ~174,809 sqm in Gangseo-gu per Yonhap/2016 and MOTIE regional-dispersion announcements; greater-Busan datacenters employed ~50 people as of 2025 (Microsoft fact sheet).

name: Microsoft Busan Data Center 2 (Miumsandan AI datacenter)
notes: Second and larger Microsoft datacenter in Busan, unveiled 23 Sep 2024 in the International Industrial Logistics City, Gangseo-gu (Miumsandan); designed to support AI-powered cloud services across Asia-Pacific. No public MW figure; part of Microsoft's multi-DC Gangseo campus. K-water signed Korea's first water-use partnership tied to Microsoft's Seoul/Busan datacenter operations in 2025.

name: LG CNS Busan Global Cloud Data Center (Mieum)
notes: LG CNS Busan data center at 153 Mieumsandan-ro, Gangseo-gu (Gurang-dong/Mieum Industrial Estate); fully operational since 2013 and at the time Korea's largest data center; part of the Gangseo cloud datacenter cluster. MOU with NTT to attract Japanese enterprise tenants. Capacity not published; LG CNS also operates Seoul, Sangam and Gasan global cloud data centers.

name: OneAsia Network Busan Data Center
notes: OneAsia Network's first South Korea data center, at Mieum Industrial Park in the Busan-Jinhae Free Economic Zone (BJFEZ), Gangseo-gu; site area ~76,000 sqm with ~100 MW IT power capacity, dual power feed, AI supercomputing infrastructure and immersion cooling; groundbreaking Feb 2024; market reports expected operational status by Q4 2025 (completion not independently confirmed).

name: Eco Delta City Green Data Center Cluster (Myeongji-dong)
developer: Busan Eco Delta Green Data Center PFV; Empyrion DC consortium; BEP & Mirae Asset consortium; Ellis Group
notes: City-designated green data center cluster on a 177,080 sqm data-industry site in Eco Delta City, Gangseo-gu (Myeongji-dong). Feb 2024 MOU with 4 anchor investors (Busan Eco Delta Green DC PFV, Empyrion DC consortium, BEP&Mirae Asset consortium, Ellis Group) for KRW 3.6 trillion to build ~5 green data centers (~100,000 servers); land contracts completed, construction planned from 2025 with full operation targeted H2 2027; KT signed a business agreement with the EDC green DC operator Apr 2025. City estimates cluster could draw up to ~360 MW at full operation (300 MW per some trade reports); KEPCO building a 1,000 MW substation in Gangseo-gu (completion 2027). Feb 2026: 1.22M sqm in Eco Delta City designated a Data Center Opportunity Development Zone (14 firms, KRW 5.36 trillion planned, 500 MW-scale shared receiving substation).

name: EGIS Asset Management AI Data Center (Myeongji-Noksan National Industrial Complex)
notes: MOU signed 17 Jun 2025 between Busan city and EGIS Asset Management to invest KRW 1.8 trillion to build two large AI-specialized data centers (10-story and 13-story buildings) at the Myeongji-Noksan National Industrial Complex (Noksan-dong, Gangseo-gu); 300+ direct jobs and ~7,570 total employment effect expected; groundbreaking targeted 2026. ~105 MW reported by trade blogs (unverified); capacity not confirmed by official sources.

name: BNK Financial Group Data Center
notes: BNK Financial Group's data center, built at the International Industrial Logistics City cloud-datacenter cluster in Gangseo-gu (per Yonhap May 2016 reporting alongside LG CNS and Daum Kakao as cluster tenants); Busan Ilbo (Apr 2026) confirms BNK Financial Group already built and operates a data center in Busan. Capacity not published.

name: Digital Edge DC PUS1 (Centum City)
notes: Digital Edge PUS1 colocation data center at 32 Centum 7-ro, Centum City, Haeundae-gu; described as the only data center in Korea integrated with a Cable Landing Station (direct international/domestic network interconnection, including to Busan's submarine cable landings); provides geographical redundancy to Seoul. Capacity not published.

notes.name: Koscom Busan Data Center
notes.notes: Koscom data center facility at 15, Jahseong-ro 133 beon-gil, Dong-gu, Busan (KRX exchange ecosystem / securities computing colocation). Listed as an operating Busan facility by datacenterHawk; no public capacity or project announcements found in this review.

notes.name: KT Busan IDC (KTICC, Busan Station)
notes.notes: KT operates a Busan IDC/colocation point at the Busan Telephone Information Center (Jung-gu, Jungang-dong 4-ga 75, near Busan Station; KTICC) and a Busan disaster-recovery (DR) center interconnected with Seoul main IDC (kt-bizinternet); Busan Ilbo (Apr 2026) lists KT among operators that already built and are running data centers in Busan. Small/medium facility; capacity not published.

notes.name: LG U+ Busan IDC
notes.notes: LG U+ operates 1 data center in Busan and lists 1 planned hyperscale-capable location in the Busan market (datacenterHawk); the operator runs 16 IDCs nationwide. Exact Busan district not confirmed by sources found in this review.

notes.name: SK Broadband Busan Data Center
notes.notes: SK Broadband (Busan) was selected by Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) in Oct 2023 as one of 7 additional 'data center regional dispersion projects' to decentralize capacity from Seoul; progress monitored under MOTIE's regional-dispersion program. Exact district within Busan not confirmed by sources found.

No datacenter projects found in Gijang-gun. Context: Gijang hosts Busan's nuclear power generation (Kori/Shin-Kori complex) and was selected (2026) as the site of Korea's first i-SMR (KHNP small modular reactor), explicitly to supply power for AI data center demand; future DC siting potential only.
